article.name: Hivemind (Lesur)
article.summary: Hivemind is a self-hosted MCP service that organizes agent memory into short-lived notes, an editable Markdown project bank, and a derived graph/vector index. The tiers have different write and authority rules: SHORT captures activity, MID is the project handbook, and LONG helps discover related historical context but is non-authoritative. This review is source-based; no runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run.

who_what.text: The official README describes a vendor-neutral, self-hosted MCP service for shared agent memory; it includes the Hivemind core, a WAF, and an embedded LONG graph-memory service. The README credits Christophe Lesur as the creator of Hivemind and its original memory engines. Hivemind is a deployable service with a Python maintenance CLI, not only a client-side memory library.

architecture.text: The product separates three horizons. SHORT stores timestamped Markdown note objects per space, with note category, content, tags, and authenticated agent identity. MID stores project handbook files as Markdown plus rules and operational metadata. LONG projects source documents and retained MID captures into graph entities/relations and chunk embeddings. A space_id is the project unit across these tiers; LONG remains a derived discovery index rather than the authority for project state.

SHORT writes create unique timestamp/agent/category/UUID filenames, avoiding overwrite conflicts between concurrent note writers. MID consolidation reads rules, prior residual summary, selected notes, and current bank; the configured model returns structured edit operations and note dispositions. The application validates and applies those operations to Markdown files, and records processing counters. LONG uses an embedded Graph Memory service with Neo4j graph records and Qdrant chunks; source paths and hashes connect derived records to source documents.

The top-level project contract says short, mid, long, and hive are separate engine ports. MID writes route through a write sink; shared-space changes pass through Hivemind's serialized commit path. The LONG engine consumes committed MID state, but LONG does not decide commits, rollback, membership, audit, tombstones, watermarks, backup, or recovery.

behavior.text: Write: agents call short_note (historically live_note) with a space, category, content, and optional tags. Agent identity is derived from the bearer token, and the service appends a new object rather than editing a prior note. The normal integration guide recommends short notes for durable decisions, observations, questions, and work summaries.

Update and consolidation: mid_consolidate queues an asynchronous per-space operation. By default a writer consolidates its own notes; selecting another agent or all agents requires manage-level authorization. One job at a time runs per space. The model proposes per-file edits/dispositions, and the implementation validates the response before writes. Processed notes are deleted only after the corresponding successful work; partial results and retained notes are reported for retry/diagnosis. Direct MID write and delete tools are available to managers, with destructive deletion requiring confirm=true.

Delete: SHORT notes have no ordinary single-note delete operation in the inspected agent tool set; administrative garbage collection is a separate maintenance path. MID provides confirmed file deletion, but deletion is subject to the write-sink route and is not a general guarantee about copies in backups or derived LONG indexes. Space deletion is an explicit destructive operator action. LONG supports document and memory lifecycle tools, including document deletion, while archive projection maintains independently retained MID preimages; source deletion, graph cleanup, backups, and restored copies therefore have distinct lifecycle boundaries.

Retrieval: SHORT reads newest-first with category, agent, and since filters; short_search is case-insensitive substring search over note content and also sorts newest-first. MID can list/read one or all Markdown bank files. LONG query embeds the query and searches graph and vector projections without a generative chat completion; graph entity search uses full-text search with a CONTAINS fallback, and vector search validates the memory namespace on returned payloads. Returned long passages include source section context and document metadata, but callers must consult the current MID source for authoritative current state.

Scope: within one deployment, tool access checks the authenticated token's space allowlist and permission level; space_id is validated before access. The official security contract is explicit that the OSS product is mono-tenant and a space allowlist is not a tenant boundary. Project Mesh can coordinate one logical project across two paired deployments, using signed invitations and full-mesh all-ACK writes; it does not claim quorum semantics, offline CRDT merging, or multi-tenant isolation.

Provenance and evidence: SHORT note metadata records agent identity, timestamp, category, tags, and space; Hivemind-specific provenance enrichment can attach origin information. Consolidation preserves disposition counters and application history, but the inspected contract does not make model-written handbook claims independently true. LONG documents retain source path, source hash, ingestion status, and chunk/section context, and graph relations identify their actual endpoints and direction. These fields help locate source material; they do not certify that extracted claims are entailed or current.

Efficiency and observability: SHORT read/search scan objects under a space prefix and then filter/sort in application code. Consolidation is batched, has asynchronous status/queue reporting and per-job counters, and different spaces can run concurrently while one space is serialized. LONG uses graph full-text indexes and vector search; source exposes namespace-specific collection identity and bounded result limits. The service provides health, status, and audit surfaces, while some job/audit views are process-local or diagnostic rather than durable records. No latency, token, cost, or storage efficiency was measured here.

metrics.text: Answerable retrieval and abstention — unmeasured. SHORT text search and LONG hybrid graph/vector retrieval exist; no answer or abstention workload was scored.
Correction accuracy and stale-value rate — unmeasured. MID allows structured edits and direct manager changes; no correction challenge set was run.
Deletion leakage — unmeasured. Note, bank, document, space, and retained backup lifecycles are separate; no deletion or restore probe was run.
Scope-isolation leakage — unmeasured. The product documents space access checks and a mono-tenant deployment boundary; no cross-space or cross-deployment probe was run.
Evidence support precision and citation coverage — unmeasured. LONG retains source metadata and section context; no extracted claim was adjudicated against source evidence.
Retrieval latency and write-to-recall delay — unmeasured. The code exposes statuses and operation counters; no workload was timed.
Tokens, cost, and storage efficiency — unmeasured. Consolidation and embeddings may use configured inference services, but no token/cost totals or storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: This review inspected the pinned README and selected architecture, SHORT, MID, LONG, auth, and deployment-contract paths. It does not exhaustively review every operator path, provider adapter, or deployment configuration.

Hivemind, its tests, and benchmark workloads were not run. Source review cannot establish deployed correctness, answer quality, cross-space isolation, physical erasure across backups, latency, token use, cost, or storage efficiency.

The source and docs describe different operational authorities across SHORT, MID, and LONG. In particular, LONG is explicitly derived and non-authoritative; current project decisions should be checked in current MID files and recent SHORT notes.
OSS is mono-tenant. Token space allowlists restrict accessible spaces for a credential but do not create tenant isolation between unrelated customers sharing one deployment.
The inspected retrieval source returns source references and context but does not establish semantic correctness of extraction, completeness of retrieved evidence, or model abstention behavior.

benchmark.note: No Hivemind runtime, tests, or benchmark workload was executed. Source observations are not measurements, and no metric values are produced.
